skill.name: data-engineering-data-driven-feature
skill.description: Build features guided by data insights, A/B testing, and continuous measurement using specialized agents for analysis, implementation, and experimentation.
skill.summary: Guide feature teams through data analysis, experiment design, implementation, rollout, and post-launch measurement.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Feature teams often ship changes without clear evidence or measurable outcomes. This skill guides analysis, A/B testing, instrumentation, rollout, and post-launch review.
actual_capabilities: Guides exploratory data analysis before feature planning.
Defines success metrics, hypotheses, and experiment design steps.
Plans analytics events, data pipelines, and warehouse integration.
Coordinates backend, frontend, and ML implementation with instrumentation.
Outlines rollout, monitoring, statistical analysis, and business review.
limitations: Requires access to real product data, metrics, and analytics tools.
Does not provide executable analytics code or dashboard templates.
Depends on compatible specialized agents for delegated implementation steps.
Cannot validate statistical conclusions without experiment data.

use_cases.title: Plan a Measured Product Feature
use_cases.description: Turn a feature idea into hypotheses, metrics, sample-size planning, and a controlled rollout path.

use_cases.title: Design Analytics Instrumentation
use_cases.description: Create event schemas, funnel tracking, and data pipeline requirements before engineers begin implementation.

use_cases.title: Assess Experiment Results
use_cases.description: Review A/B test outcomes, segment effects, guardrail metrics, and business impact for a rollout decision.

prompt_templates.title: Start Feature Discovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to evaluate a proposed feature. Identify available data, baseline metrics, user segments, and missing inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Experiment
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for A/B test planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design an A/B test for a feature. Include hypotheses, success metrics, guardrails, sample size needs, and rollout stages.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Instrumented Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan implementation for a data-driven feature. Cover feature flags, analytics events, pipelines, monitoring, and validation.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Launch Outcomes
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request after experiment data is available.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to assess experiment results. Compare statistical impact, business value, segment behavior, guardrail metrics, and next actions.

output_examples.input: Evaluate a new onboarding checklist for paid account activation.
output_examples.output: A plan with baseline activation metrics, target segments, experiment hypotheses, tracking events, rollout steps, and decision criteria.

output_examples.input: Prepare analytics for a personalized recommendation feature.
output_examples.output: An instrumentation plan covering exposure events, interaction events, conversion funnels, cohort analysis, and monitoring requirements.

output_examples.input: Review A/B test results for a pricing page change.
output_examples.output: A decision memo comparing conversion lift, confidence intervals, revenue impact, guardrail metrics, and recommended rollout action.

best_practices: Define primary metrics and guardrail metrics before implementation starts.
Validate event quality in staging before sending production traffic.
Use gradual rollout and rollback rules for every experiment.
anti_patterns: Do not choose metrics after reviewing experiment results.
Do not launch variants without validating randomization and sample size.
Do not treat analytics tracking as a post-launch task.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create a data-backed feature plan from discovery through experiment analysis.

faq.question: Does it require existing analytics data?
faq.answer: Existing data is strongly recommended because the workflow starts with baseline behavior and metrics.

faq.question: Can it support A/B testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes experiment design, feature flags, rollout planning, monitoring, and statistical analysis.

faq.question: Does it implement code directly?
faq.answer: It provides implementation guidance and agent prompts, but it does not include executable source code.

faq.question: Which teams benefit from it?
faq.answer: Product, data, engineering, analytics, and growth teams can use it for measured feature delivery.

faq.question: Can it replace statistical review?
faq.answer: No. It structures the review process, but final conclusions need valid data and qualified analysis.
